item.title: France suspends stun grenade use at student protests after pupil loses hand
item.description:
Minister says use of grenades has been stopped after a student lost a hand as protests across France continue How dilapidated are French schools and how bad is inequality in the education system? France’s interior minister has suspended the use of stun grenades by police at high school demonstrations but rejected mounting accusations of police brutality during two weeks of protests marred by often violent clashes that have injured hundreds. Laurent Nuñez told RTL radio on Wednesday that he had ordered a temporary halt on the use of the grenades “in the context of the high school students’ movement” after a 15-year-old boy lost a hand during a protest in Lens, northern France, on Monday. item.title: Russia: WHO not able to 'fully' assess plague situation
item.description:
This article was featured in the One Story to Read Today newsletter. Sign up for it here. The scenario is right out of a Stephen King novel: At a medical lab stashed away in a remote Siberian city, a pretty young technician was exposed to a deadly pathogen. She died, the lab went into lockdown , and soon rumors emerged that the Russian security services were on the scene. Now the world waits to see whether some monstrous microbe is going to make its way out of Russia’s forests. What’s going on in Russia is bad, but—at least so far—not that bad. We know that someone working at a research institute that studies various forms of plague has died of pneumonia, which suggests that she mishandled a sample of pneumonic plague. That’s about it. item.title: Scars from Oct. 7 fuel deep divisions over Netanyahu ahead of Israeli election
item.description:
Israel is marking the third anniversary of the Oct. 7 terror attacks three weeks before an election where Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's personal culpability for the country's worst-ever security failure will be a central issue. Why it matters: Netanyahu has never looked more politically vulnerable than in the weeks after Oct. 7, but he has defied expectations by keeping his government afloat — presiding over simultaneous wars and an atmosphere of perpetual emergency. Though the polls are tight, they leave a clear path for the ultimate political survivor to hang on yet again. But Oct. 7 still looms over the country and his candidacy. The opposition lambasts him for refusing to take responsibility or allow an independent inquiry into the Hamas attacks that killed around 1,200 people. item.title: What we know about espionage, treason allegations against Germany's ex-spy chief
item.description:
The former head of Germany’s foreign intelligence service was arrested Tuesday on suspicion of treason and conducting espionage on behalf of foreign governments, in a major blow to Berlin’s security establishment. Though the BND has historically been plagued by spying scandals — deterring some Western partners from sharing intelligence — August Hanning, who left the agency in 2005, is its first former chief to face charges . The revelations add pressure on an intelligence establishment trying to remake itself after decades, and complicate Berlin’s efforts to counter Russia’s hybrid war, as lawmakers debate expanding the BND’s powers . But a ruling party lawmaker cast the arrest in a positive light, telling DW it shows that Germany “ will not tolerate the betrayal of secrets .” — Brendan Ruberry

item.title: ABC and Trump's FCC battle in federal court over free speech and jurisdiction issues
item.description:
I thought I'd pass along the amicus brief that I just filed yesterday on behalf of Prof. Rebecca Roiphe (an expert in the law governing lawyers), Prof. Nadine Strossen (a free speech scholar and former President of the ACLU), and myself, supporting the cert. petition in Eastman v. State Bar (the decision below is here ). The brief seeks to explain to the Court why the underlying legal issues in this case are important and merit the Court's granting review. Like most other amicus briefs supporting petitions for review, it doesn't seek to argue about the truth or falsity of petitioner's statements: The Court generally grants review to resolve conflicts about what the right legal rule should be, not to resolve factual disputes.
